chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from more than one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
severing the head of the dead is more severe than severing the head of the living.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on severing the head of a corpse compared to a living person?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to clarify that severing the head of a corpse carries greater legal weight than doing so to a living person, likely due to the distinct nature of the injury to the body's integrity after death. This specific comparison highlights the nuanced Shia jurisprudence on *diya* (blood money), distinguishing between the sanctity of the living body and the residual honor of the deceased. The ruling underscores the principle that post-mortem mutilation is a distinct violation of bodily rights, warranting specific compensation calculations.
